results.reason: Issue 3 says the First Supplement window ran on September 28 and Buyer did not terminate. It explains that §5.7(c) deems the Ferrovane-related inaccuracies cured for Article IX and §7.2(a) and waives termination. It concludes Buyer has no indemnity for the customer loss.

Issue 4 contrasts the Escrow 'actual out-of-pocket' definition, which excludes diminution in value, lost profits and attorneys' fees, with the broader SPA definition. It cites Escrow §4.3 and explains that SPA §11.11 lets the Escrow Agreement control disbursement mechanics, cutting recoveries from the escrow.

Issue 1 says a >50% voting equity acquisition is a deemed assignment requiring Tavinor's consent under MSA §14.2, and the 100% purchase triggers it. It notes Annex 7.2(d) lists only the lender payoff, and §4.4, §7.2(d) and §5.3 do not cover the consent. It flags termination or List Price repricing, plus the 85% requirements commitment and difficulty replacing the supplier.
States the 10-Business-Day period from the September 14 delivery ran on September 28, which is before the October 13 letter.
States the escrow is $4.85M (10% of price), which equals $4,850,000.
Formatted as a memorandum to the Partner. Each issue gives document-and-section locations ('Where'), explains why it matters, and gives a recommended fix or position.
Includes 'Things I could not resolve from the documents' and 'Needed from the client' sections, plus per-issue open and client-input notes.
Says termination for Ferrovane was waived and the window passed. It does not claim the right is still live.
Expressly states the Tavinor consent is not in Annex 7.2(d) and is not a closing condition.
